BiblicalUsage: An oar is what a galley uses, and a scourge is what an overflowing flood is called. Isaiah hears men trusting that when the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come unto them, because they made lies their refuge. But the same prophet promises a place of broad rivers where no galley with oars shall go, and no gallant ship pass by.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two pictures answer each other, for men trust lies against the scourge while God promises a river no enemy ship can sail, and I hold that His protection is the only refuge that holds.
